To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have contributed 1,000 protein crystal structures to the public domain, including 300 structures that are of high resolution, and that these structures have contributed significantly to the understanding of biology.

we have contributed to the NIH-National Institute of General Medical Sciences (NIGMS) Protein Structure Initiative (PSI) by developing methods and tools to facilitate the structural genomics pipeline, including protein expression and purification, protein production and crystallization, and structure solution, and by contributing to the PSI Knowledgebase (PKB) to support the PSI.

the NIH-NIGMSPSIProduction Centers have contributed 1,500 high-resolution structures, 1,200 medium-resolution structures, and >2,300 structures of protein complexes to the global effort to understand biology through structure determination.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural characterization of proteins, the development of methods and tools to facilitate such characterization, and the use of structural information in the context of biology and biomedicine.
elucidating protein structures at the atomic scale, and the application of these data to understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying biological processes and human disease.
the development, implementation, and application of high-throughput methods to solve protein structures and to understand the relationship between protein structure and function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the structural biology community has made significant contributions in the past 10 years to the understanding of biological processes, to drug discovery and to the understanding of the molecular basis of human diseases.
high-throughput methods, including structural biology, have transformed the way we study biology, and in particular, the way we study proteins.
the Protein Structure Initiative (PSI) was a success.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have been successful in achieving our primary goal of developing high-throughput methods for structural genomics, and we have been successful, in a limited way, in achieving a secondary goal of using these methods and technologies to study the structure and function of a wide range of proteins.
structural genomics has made a substantial and lasting impact in biology and human health, and that the Protein Structure Initiative (PSI) has been a major driver of this impact.

the NIH-NIGM Structural Genomics Centers have contributed to the NIH-NIAMS Protein Structure Initiative (PSI) by developing new methods and technologies, and applying them to the determination of the 3D structures of proteins and protein complexes that have been difficult to obtain by more traditional methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the structural genomics community, through the National Institutes of Health National Institute of General Medical Sciences Protein Structure Initiative, has contributed to our understanding of biology through the structural characterization of proteins.

the structural genomics community, through the NIH-NIGMI-supported Protein Structure Initiative (PSI) and other structural genomics efforts, has made a significant contribution to our understanding of biology by providing the structural community with a large and growing set of protein structures.
structural genomics has been successful.
